title: Portable call-rewrite proxy — brain dump
content:
Quick brain-dump / working spec for a lightweight, portable call-rewrite proxy that can sit in client-side adapters, edge proxies, or in private-runner edge components. Goal: make tool/function invocation semantics portable across trust boundaries while preserving observability, auth mappings, and resumable streaming.

Context and motivation:
- Multiple places in the stack may need to rewrite or mediate outgoing tool calls: client-side adapters, edge proxies, gateway, or on-host private-runner.
- Current patterns are ad-hoc: host proxies do rewrites inside gateway code, client libs do local rewrites, private runners require special-case wiring.
- We want a small, opinionated contract so components can:
  - annotate and forward tool invocations
  - rewrite endpoints/args based on policy (e.g., redact, replace, route to a tenant-local tool provider)
  - preserve streaming and checkpoint-resume semantics
  - attach verifiable provenance for audit/forensics without leaking secrets

Design goals (prioritized):
1) Minimal surface area: single JSON-wire contract for request/response + optional streaming frames.
2) Composable: upstream can add rewrite rules without modifying downstream runners.
3) Secure-by-default: no accidental credential forwarding; explicit credential binding and scoped tokens.
4) Resumable: support fragment-level resume for long-running tool outputs.
5) Observable: attach compact provenance and tracing hooks (span ids, rewrite version).
6) Portable: implementable in small Go/Rust binary (edge) or lightweight JS shim in clients.

High-level flow (happy path):
1) Client issues an LLM response that includes a tool call request (name, args, call_id).
2) Ingress adapter wraps the call in a "portable-call" envelope and POSTs to rewrite-proxy endpoint.
3) Rewrite-proxy consults local policy (static or remote) and returns either: allow (possibly rewritten target), deny, or transform.
4) If allowed, proxy forwards the envelope to resolved tool endpoint. For streaming outputs, the proxy establishes a streaming channel (chunk frames) and maps chunk ids to original call_id.
5) Downstream runner returns results; proxy re-encapsulates into the expected LLM-tool-response envelope and returns to caller.

Envelope (wire shape) — sketch (NOT final):
{
  "envelope_version": "v1",
  "call_id": "string",            // stable id for resume/trace
  "origin": {                   // who originated the call (low-trust)
    "client_id": "string",
    "session_id": "string",
    "span_id": "string"
  },
  "tool": {
    "name": "string",
    "args": "object-as-json-string",
    "metadata": {"declared_privacy": "public|sensitive|secret"}  // hint for rewrite
  },
  "auth": {                    // optional: explicit credential tokens (scoped)
    "type": "bearer|signed-claim|none",
    "token_id": "string",     // opaque id not raw secret (see binding below)
    "scopes": ["string"]
  },
  "rewrite_hint": {"policy_version": "string", "ruleset_id": "string"},
  "trace": {"trace_id": "string", "parent_span": "string"}
}

Notes on the envelope:
- args field is intentionally stringified JSON to avoid schema explosion on the proxy side; proxies can peek and transform with pluggable parsers.
- auth.token_id should map to a local credential vault entry; the proxy must not forward raw credentials unless explicitly allowed by policy.
- provenance added by proxies should include rewrite_version and a short HMAC over the rewrite decision + call_id (verifiable by internal tooling).

Config sketch for rewrite-proxy (local policy file) — example:
rewrite-config.yaml (concept):
- ruleset_id: "default-tenant-safe"
  priority: 100
  match:
    tool_name: "ssh.exec"
    declared_privacy: ["sensitive", "secret"]
  action: "deny"
  reason: "no-ssh-from-client"

- ruleset_id: "local-file-run"
  priority: 50
  match:
    tool_name: "fs.read"
    origin.client_id: ["local-agent-v2"]
  action: "rewrite"
  rewrite:
    target: "file-provider.local/v1/read"
    arg_map: {"path": "path", "mode": "mode"}
  auth_binding: "local-kv:read-only"

Auth binding model (notes):
- Binding layer maps token_id -> credential artifact (HSM/KMS reference or ephemeral short-lived token).
- Proxy may request a delegated ephemeral credential from credential broker (via mTLS).
- All requests performed on behalf of the origin must carry a purpose string that is auditable.

Streaming semantics (fragment resume):
- For streaming tool outputs (e.g., long file downloads, live shell output), use frame envelope:
  - FRAME_START {call_id, frame_id, seq=0, meta...}
  - FRAME_DATA  {call_id, frame_id, seq=N, chunk: base64}
  - FRAME_ACK   {call_id, frame_id, seq=N}
  - FRAME_END   {call_id, frame_id, final_meta}
- The proxy persists minimal resume state: last-acked seq per frame_id. On reconnect client sends resume request with last_seq to continue.
- Keep frames idempotent-looking: attach monotonic seq + HMAC to allow detection of duplicate frames.

Observability & audit fields to include in responses:
- rewrite_provenance: "rs:default-tenant-safe@2025-11-10:allow"
- rewrite_signature: base64(hmac)  // short, verifiable by infra team tools
- audit_uri: internal link to audit event (LIN-6721)

Edge cases / open questions (todo):
- Should the proxy accept raw binary args or only JSON? (prefer JSON/string to simplify parsing).
- How to handle large binary artifacts (files): support pre-signed URLs via a file-provider pattern or chunked frames?
- Credential TTLs: enforce short TTLs; require delegation via broker for cross-tenant calls.
- How to represent function/tool capability versioning? (tool_name:v2)
- Backpressure model for proxy when downstream tool is slow: propagate 503-with-retry-metadata vs queue in-proxy?
- Rate-limiting: should be pluggable by origin client or solely per-proxy tenant policy?

Implementation plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (experiment): JS shim that lives in client SDK. Minimal policy: local map of tool_name->target. No credential forwarding. Logs proof-of-concept to GH PR linked.
- Phase 1 (edge binary): small Go service that supports envelope v1, local YAML policy, streaming frames, and a credential-binding interface that calls credential-broker (mTLS). Deploy as Docker sidecar on private-runner.
- Phase 2 (gateway integration): allow gateway to call the same binary as a plugin/sidecar; provide remote policy distribution and metrics/trace hooks.

Compatibility notes:
- Keep envelope versioned; make v1 intentionally conservative. Add field for "capabilities" describing supported frame types.
- Try to reuse existing tracing ids (OpenTelemetry) and add a small shim to map proxy provenance to our event model.

Short ASCII architecture sketch:

[client-lib] --(portable-call envelope)--> [local-shim-js] --(optional)--> [edge-proxy/rewrite] --(resolved endpoint call)--> [tool-provider]

Where "local-shim-js" may be a no-op in many deployments; "edge-proxy/rewrite" is the binary that enforces policies and performs rewrite/auth binding.

Acceptance criteria for phase 1:
- Can rewrite fs.read -> file-provider.local and enforce auth_binding.
- Resume streaming test passes with simulated disconnects (client resume from seq).
- Policy change rollouts (yaml swap + health check) do not drop in-flight calls; old calls keep old rewrite_provenance.

Small list of follow-ups / action items:
- Lina: prototype JS shim that converts our internal tool-call shape to envelope v1 (LIN-6721).
- Marco: spike on HMAC provenance format + credential-broker handshake (PR #482).
- Me (Samir): write a minimal wiring spec for gateway plugin and a smoke test harness.

Random notes / heuristics I wanted to capture:
- Keep the rewrite decision compact and signed so auditors can easily link a tool call to the applied policy without loading large logs.
- Prefer explicit token_id bindings over blindly forwarding raw tokens. The proxy should be the only thing that can request ephemeral credentials when policy permits.
- Aim for a small, well-tested core (frames + envelope + auth-binding API) and then provide adapters for common languages.

References / example artifacts:
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress-proxy/pull/482 (early shim + test harness)
- Linear: LIN-6721 (policy rollout + audit requirements)

End of dump. This is rough — intended as an iterative spec to share with Lina/Marco and land a mini-prototype.
